title: libds allocator routing
preamble:
# libds allocator routing

How libds routes heap allocation — its own C
code and every vendored C library that allocates — through a single layer that an
integrator may redirect to their own allocator with **no per-call
function-pointer indirection**, bound either at compile time (a macro
layer) or at link time (weak symbols), selected by one build flag. It
realises the [IDAT.1] ownership model and binds the source, build,
symbol, and public-ABI shapes inside libds.

Prefix `IALC`.

Takes as fixed:
- **[IDAT.1]** — `ds_result_t` at every call site, per-object `malloc`
  with single ownership, per-engine state (no globals), caller-owned
  `const char *`. This spec routes that allocation; it does not change
  the ownership model.
- **The public ABI** (`runtime/include/libds.h`) — this spec does not
  change it; the one symbol it owns there is `ds_free` ([IALC.4]).
- **The libc chokepoint** — every allocation in libds's C code and
  protobuf-c bottoms out at libc `malloc`/`calloc`/`realloc`/`free`
  (+ `strdup`/`strndup`); no aligned-alloc family is used. The regex
  engine allocates through C++'s global `operator new` instead, and is
  outside the layer ([IALC.3.5]).

## What this is not

- **Not a conforming-runtime contract.** Allocation routing is internal
  to libds; another runtime is unaffected, and nothing here binds one.
- **Not an error-number registry.** No new error code: an allocation
  failure surfaces as the existing `DS_ERR_OOM`.
- **Not the integrator memory-ownership contract** — that is the
  callback contract ([NCBK]). This
  spec is the *internal* routing that makes a custom allocator total.
